newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan oil retailers seek slow liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan oil retailers seek slow liberalisation.

text.p: Venezuelan gasoline distributors and retailers asked Congress on Wednesday to slow the speed of liberalisation in the domestic gasoline market.
Venezuela's gasoline prices are currently equivalent to about 80 percent of the world price and reforms under discussion would put them nearer the true cost of delivering fuel to the consumer.
Roger Melendez, president of business group Fenegas, asked for an introductory period of one year to ensure a gradual increase in prices.

According to current plans, he said, "The hidden costs and state subsidies would be transferred immediately to the supply network and the losses which Petroleos de Venezuela makes would be transferred suddenly to the consuming public."
Melendez was attending a special congressional committee studying the reforms.
The committee is preparing a document to be discussed by the chamber while the government plans to present its own plans within the next two weeks and says Congress' proposal is too statist.
Venezuelan businessmen asked that the market be opened first to Venezuelan and then to international companies.
Fenegas members run 1,400 gasoline stations under franchise from PDVSA out of the total 1,600 stations in the country.
